# Joint cap-trace compactification and the ordinary boundary-stress limit

This note records exactly what survives the vanishing-buffer limit without
silently replacing a SAME-dual critical menu. The base coefficients of the
actual menu may diverge. An archived trace-preserving clamp supplies bounded
AUXILIARY records for individual caps; joint boundary and section measures
then retain their original selections and weights.

The conclusion is an ordinary cap stress, with allocated supporting sections
and, for surviving groups, balanced continuous normals and a common allocated
section centroid. It does not assert preservation of a projected group-cover
resultant, a finite critical-menu selection with the same stress, an affine
centroid graph, or a Gamma payment.

The finite-base clamp is already proved in Section 2 of
`candidate 4e12bc9cd7731df3` and its
referenced triangle source. The new bookkeeping here is its use as a record
map for the joint SAME-selector measures and their local Gauss--Green identity.
The small correction estimate comes from
`candidate 79036a0d1b9e182a` and
`candidate e2b434a53584fe7e`.

## 1. Geometric and measure setup

Let P be finite and fixed. Suppose K_z^j converge in Hausdorff distance to
positive convex K_z, all contained in B(0,R), with uniform inballs. The
covariances Sigma_j converge to a positive matrix Sigma. Every selected
nonvertical cap has continuous normal u satisfying

    u^T Sigma_j u=1.

Thus 0<u_min<=|u|<=u_max uniformly. Write a cap as

    H={a.z+u.X>=c},  tau_z=c-a.z.

Each actual cap has raw mixed mass Q_j, where Q_j tends to Q. Its inward
body selector s_H is one on boundary points with strict positive cap margin,
zero on strict negative margin, and lies in [0,1] on a supporting facet.
The associated section measure lambda_(H,z) has coarea normalization
dH_(d-1)/|u| on a proper section. On an inside-supporting facet its density
is (1-s_H)/|u|; on an outside-supporting facet it is s_H/|u|. It is zero for
a strictly full or strictly empty fiber. These are the actual allocated
selectors supplied by the dual, not independently chosen indicators.

In the conservative construction the current inside allocation is zero,
but its limiting allocation need not be zero; Section 7 gives an exact
example. On a current outside facet both allocations agree.

The cap weights omega_H are nonnegative and sum to one. A uniformly bounded
number of group labels can be retained; the number of caps within a group
need not be uniformly bounded. Atomic rows, if present, can be recorded
separately by their finitely many whole-fiber patterns. In the intended
small-buffer application the uniform base gap has already removed them.

## 2. Bounded individual records, without changing the actual menu

Choose H_*>u_max R+1. For each original cap keep every tau_z lying in
[-H_*,H_*] EXACTLY. For tau_z>H_* require the new threshold to be at least
H_*; for tau_z<-H_* require it to be at most -H_*. These are linear
constraints on (c_hat,a_hat), with a fixed finite matrix having rows
(1,-z). They are feasible because the original coefficients are feasible.

Take the minimum Euclidean norm feasible vector, after removing directions
invisible on P. Its norm is bounded by C(P)H_* uniformly. Indeed at the
minimum it is orthogonal to the kernel of all active rows: both small
directions in that kernel remain feasible. Choose an independent active-row
basis R_I. The minimum is therefore

    R_I^T (R_I R_I^T)^(-1) b_I.

All entries of b_I have absolute value at most H_*, and only finitely many
row bases occur. This proves the bound, including deficient base rank.

The cap (a_hat,u,c_hat) has exactly the same set trace on EVERY old fiber.
Every proper or supporting cut threshold is unchanged; all other thresholds
remain strictly outside the common support range. Consequently it has the
same actual mass, body selector, section measure, coarea and section moments.
Its margin value at any own-proper source contact is also unchanged.

We use this as a RECORD of the old cap and its existing measures. We do not
substitute it into a moving covering construction, assert preservation of
sum rho a, or replace the original free-normal response controls. Those
assertions would require separate proofs. The compact record space A is
the bounded closed space of (a_hat,u,c_hat) with u_min<=|u|<=u_max.

## 3. Joint measures and the limiting allocated cap

Let s_j be the physical boundary measure on the finite disjoint union of
fibers, with (z,X,n_Kzj(X)) recorded. It converges weakly to s_0. A common
radial parametrization proves this: convex gauges and their gradients
converge a.e., while the uniform inball bounds the surface Jacobians.

For one group, define measures

    Lambda_j=sum_H omega_H delta_(record H),
    eta_j=sum_H omega_H delta_(record H) times s_H ds_j,
    zeta_j=sum_H omega_H delta_(record H) times
                                      sum_z lambda_(H,z).

All are on fixed compact spaces. We have

    0<=eta_j<=Lambda_j tensor s_j,
    marginal_A(zeta_j)<=S_max Lambda_j.

The coarea bound S_max is uniform, from the outer radius and u_min.
Extract a common weak subsequence. Then

    0<=eta<=Lambda tensor s_0,
    marginal_A(zeta)<=S_max Lambda.

Disintegration gives a boundary selector 0<=s_H<=1 and a positive section
measure lambda_H for Lambda-a.e. bounded cap record H. The selector is one
at strictly captured boundary points and zero at strictly excluded ones:
this follows directly on the open sets where the limiting cap margin is
bounded away from zero.

The captured-volume function is jointly continuous in the compact cap
record and the converging convex fibers, since |u|>=u_min and every cutting
hyperplane is volume-null. Hence EVERY record in the support of Lambda has

    sum_z |K_z intersect H|=Q.                         (1)

No source-dependent tilt replacement was used in this limit.

## 4. The local Gauss--Green identity closes the section selectors

For every current cap, every fiber, and every C^1 scalar test psi,

    integral_boundary(K_z^j) s_H psi n dS
      =integral_(K_z^j intersect H) grad psi dX
                              +u integral psi d lambda_(H,z). (2)

For a proper section this is Gauss--Green on the captured part. On a
supporting facet it follows from the SAME allocation rules in Section 1.
Multiply by a continuous function of the cap record and pass to the joint
weak limit. The volume term passes by its preceding joint continuity.
After disintegration, (2) holds for Lambda-a.e. limiting cap and every test
psi; a countable dense set first gives a common exceptional set.

This determines the limiting section measure completely:

* on a proper cut, lambda_(H,z)=dH_(d-1)/|u| on the actual section;
* at an inside support, lambda_(H,z)=(1-s_H)dH_(d-1)/|u| on that facet;
* at an outside support, lambda_(H,z)=s_H dH_(d-1)/|u| on that facet;
* for a strict full or empty trace it is zero.

To see uniqueness, subtract the usual captured-part Gauss--Green identity.
Away from a supporting facet the boundary selector is already fixed.
At an inside facet n=-u/|u|, so the difference is
u(1-s_H)dS/|u|; at an outside facet n=u/|u|, so it is
u s_H dS/|u|. Since u is nonzero, scalar test functions determine the
section measure. This also excludes additional singular section mass on
lower-dimensional edges. For d=1, the same proof uses endpoint counting.

In particular all zeroth and first section moments survive. Taking psi=1
and psi=X_l in (2) gives the exact ordinary identities

    integral s_H n dS =u lambda_H(K_z),
    integral s_H X tensor n dS
       =|K_z intersect H| Id
                           +(integral X d lambda_H) tensor u. (3)

There is no unproved exchange between limiting surface and volume measures.

## 5. Surviving group means and continuous-normal balance

Now retain the additional ACTUAL multicontact equations of the audited
dual. For group i,

    omega_ij T_ij=kappa_i rho_ij,
    Ybar_i=sum_a kappa_ia Y_ia/kappa_i,
    mean(lambda_ij)=Ybar_i-(e_i/kappa_i)(0,Sigma_j u_ij). (4)

Here T_ij is total coarea, sum_j rho_ij=1, and
e_i=sum_a kappa_ia delta_ia. In this section assume a FIXED FINITE contact
label set A_i for each group along the subsequence, with stabilized bases.
This is supplied by the actual package's at-most-one proper contact mark
per sampled base; finite base sites alone would not suffice if multiple
marks per base were allowed to grow without bound. Assume their marks converge and
remain in uniform own balls, and max_a delta_ia tends to zero. Every cap
of the group passes through the buffered mark of EVERY contact:

    a_ij.p_ia+u_ij.y_ia-c_ij=delta_ia.                 (5)

Equation (5) is a retained hypothesis of the actual finite-contact cover;
it is not inferred just from a cap's mass Q_j.

Uniform own section bounds give S_min<=T_ij<=S_max. Thus a positive limiting
cap-group weight eta_i implies a positive limiting kappa_i. Pass to such a
group. Its limiting coarea-weighted cap law is

    d rho_i(H)=T_H d Lambda_i(H)/kappa_i,
    T_H=lambda_H(S).

By (4), using e_i/kappa_i<=max_a delta_ia, every limiting allocated section
has the SAME full mean Ybar_i. This mean is the limit of the
kappa-weighted contact barycenter. It need not be an integer-base mark or
equal to every individual source.

The contact equations also give

    kappa_i sum_j rho_ij u_ij
       =sum_a e_ia [a_E,ia+c_ia/(N L_ia)].             (6)

The uniform source ball bounds both |a_E,ia| and |c_ia|/L_ia by 1/r_s.
Therefore (6), divided by kappa_i, tends to zero, and

    integral u d rho_i(H)=0.                          (7)

The auxiliary records preserve (5), since every own-proper threshold is
inside the strict common support range. Thus every limiting cap plane
passes through every limiting contact mark; those own sections stay proper.

Equations (1), (4), (7) are genuine ordinary cap/section conclusions. They
are ordinary CRITICAL caps when Q is the limiting ordinary maximum and the
retained marks are ordinary deepest, as supplied by the joint-minimum limit
theorem; without that extra identification they are only the proved
mass-Q, through-mark cap statements. They
even imply that the compact support of this group's cap law covers the
whole continuous plane at each of its limiting contact bases: otherwise all
u.(X-y_a) would be negative, contrary to their zero average. This is a cover
only at that group's retained contacts. It is not a claimed full covering
of every deepest base after groups of zero dual weight are discarded.

No projected base-normal balance is asserted for the auxiliary records.
Selecting a finite balanced subfamily, if desired, must not be identified
with the existing stress measure or its SAME-dual weights.

## 6. Ordinary boundary stress and what does not pass

The total body-selector measure is the marginal of eta. It has the form
w_0 ds_0 with 0<=w_0<=1. The vanishing-log theorem gives

    ||Xi_j ds_j-(W_j-beta_j)ds_j||_TV ->0.

Hence for every common bounded continuous actual test speed Phi in the
tested cones,

    integral (w_0-beta_0) Phi ds_0<=0.                 (8)

If all globally finite convex physical Phi(z,X) are admitted, (8) is the
ordinary convex-order boundary stress, with affine tests and their negatives
giving equal mass and first moment. The current exact affine-force identities
also pass with the recorded normals:

    sum_z F_z=0,  sum_z z tensor F_z=0,
    sum_z integral_boundary(K_z) (w_0-beta_0)X tensor n dS=0,
    F_z=integral_boundary(K_z) (w_0-beta_0)n dS.        (9)

The centroid-radial expression remains -sum_z g_z.F_z. It need not vanish
for a nonaffine centroid graph, and that radial array need not be an actual
compatible motion.

The tilted volume measures dm/(M L_j) need not have uniformly bounded mass.
Their source weights e_a/Delta are different from the kappa contact weights
in (4). Therefore no limiting original-volume martingale, uniform-template
lift, or centroid identity is silently attached to (8)--(9). Original-volume
row measures may be separately compactified as finite measures, but their
barycenters are not the old tilted-row barycenters. These distinctions are
exactly the remaining scope of this closure theorem.

## 7. Supporting allocations really can change in the limit

On K=[-1,1], let H_m={X>=-1+1/m}. Every cut is proper, its body selector
is zero at -1 and one at 1, and its coarea section is the point -1+1/m.
The limiting cap is inside-supporting and captures all volume, but its
limiting body selector at -1 is zero and its section selector there is one.
Thus the current inside-zero allocation convention is NOT closed under
limits. The consistent inside complement rule in Section 4 is necessary.

Similarly H_m={X>=1-1/m} converges to the outside support at 1, with both
limiting body and section selectors one there, even though the limiting cap
volume is zero. Both examples satisfy the local identity (2) exactly.

For a base-tilt example use P={-1,0,1}, all fibers [-1,1], and caps
X+m z>=0 with m>2. Replacing m by 2 preserves every sampled trace and every
coarea. It changes the base coefficient and can change a weighted base
resultant. This is why Section 2 treats the clamp as a record map, not as
an unproved replacement of the full critical-cover construction.

These examples and identities are checked in
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_joint_cap_selector_compactification_defect_transport.py`. No numerical
screen is used to infer the general measure or balance conclusions.
